title: Existing backend keeps its decisions

R1.reason: Keeps NestJS/Express, Prisma, npm and Jest; uses only the existing stack. The raw SQL fallback stays within Prisma.

R2.reason: Copies the customers module pattern: FirebaseAuthGuard, @CurrentUser, ownerId/companyId scoping, existing items/limit response keys, and registers in the existing InvoicesModule.

R3.reason: Filters by ownerId and companyId from the token in the query. The e2e test covers a colleague in the same company and a user in another company.

R4.reason: Cursor pagination with limit capped at 100, order issuedAt desc then id desc as a unique tie-breaker, and a validated cursor.

R5.reason: Keeps the { statusCode, error, message } format and the existing filter. Proposing a machine code is deferred as a separate proposal.

R6.reason: Writes e2e tests first (Red), lists cases, and states what would be run: the new e2e test fails first, then implement and run related tests. It notes nothing was run.

R7.reason: Defers the error code, Swagger and the configureApp refactor as separate proposals. But it adds a DB index and migration, a cursor design that departs from customers' offset, and a README change inside the change itself, and the answer does not label the index and cursor choice as optional.

forbidden.item: Switching to Fastify or the Fastify adapter, Drizzle, Yarn or Vitest as part of the change
forbidden.evidence: Stays on NestJS/Express, Prisma, npm and Jest; Swagger is explicitly not added.

forbidden.item: Adding a second lockfile or a second ORM
forbidden.evidence: No lockfile change; the $queryRaw fallback is still Prisma.

forbidden.item: Changing the existing error response format clients rely on
forbidden.evidence: Explicitly keeps { statusCode, error, message } and leaves HttpErrorFilter unchanged; a code field is proposed separately.

forbidden.item: Taking the user id from the query string or body
forbidden.evidence: Identity comes only from the verified token via @CurrentUser; there is no userId parameter.

grade.summary: A strong, well-scoped answer that follows the existing patterns, filters by owner and tenant, uses bounded stable cursor pagination and tests first, and violates no forbidden decision. The only weak point is that the index and migration are bundled into the change instead of being offered as optional.
